allowedWork: Stable dense endpoint diagnostics, one bounded common alignment correction, generic scene compositor evolution, and only the named split, radical, reader, and compound exemplars with focused evidence.
disallowedWork: No notation, operation, viewport, card, or expression exceptions; durable renderer state; clone semantic authority; global rollout; unrelated dirty-worktree edits; Manim, CAS, live LLM, or curriculum work.
goal: Resolve or bound the generic native KaTeX endpoint jerk, then prove inverse split, radical succession, one reader card, and one compound presentation without new lifecycle or scheduling categories.
commitCadence: Commit every independently reversible verified slice with exact path staging and its completed Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: Stop if any notation, operation, viewport, expression, or card-specific offset, matcher, lifecycle, track, or scheduler is required.
Stop if clone/native identity depends on visual equality or DOM order instead of canonical reconciliation lineage.
Stop if the endpoint correction is not one bounded common scene-level correction or changes native DOM.
Stop if any painted source or target atom is implicit, unowned, duplicated, or unstable.
Stop if DOM nodes, computed styles, geometry, tracks, keyframes, or backend plans enter durable semantic or reader artifacts.
Stop if moving clones gain accessibility, hover, focus, annotation, Cloze, or export authority.
Stop if a promoted exemplar introduces a notation or operation-specific lifecycle or scheduling category.
Stop if the retained endpoint residual grows beyond its measured bound or becomes a semantic or accessibility defect.
Stop on performance, payload, accessibility, semantic, reader, review, production, static-JS, export, seek, rewind, or responsive regression.
Stop if work broadens beyond the four named exemplars or touches unrelated dirty-worktree changes.
Stop if a required automated or visual gate fails without one bounded generic correction.

slices.title: endpoint-reproduction-harness

slices.title: endpoint-telemetry-contract

slices.title: clone-native-atom-correlation
slices.summary: Added deterministic handoff correlations from material owner IDs to native target atoms through reconciliation disposition and track identities, with explicit departing tracks and total merge/split coverage; duplicates, missing targets, and unbacked IDs fail closed.

slices.title: baseline-and-style-microscope
slices.summary: Added repeatable wide/phone/DPR glyph handoff telemetry and stable capture evidence. Track rectangles already coincide within about 0.1 CSS px; the persistent plus clone instead retains a source font roughly 1.43 times the target numerator font, causing generic paint overflow and baseline drift at handoff.

slices.title: structural-rule-microscope
slices.summary: Added generic structural rule handoff telemetry for axis, length, thickness, transforms, clipping, border style, opacity, and paint identity. Wide/phone material and native rules match in style and thickness with about 0.016 px length residual, ruling out rule geometry as the visible jerk cause.

slices.title: handoff-ownership-timing
slices.summary: Proved exclusive atomic ownership through the endpoint with reverse/direct-seek equality. At 99.9% material glyph boxes and structural rules are subpixel-close to native while the persistent plus retains a style mismatch and roughly 1.63 px maximum baseline residual, isolating the jerk to paint adaptation rather than handoff timing.

slices.title: generic-alignment-model
slices.summary: Added a pure fail-closed common-translation model. It returns a bounded correction only when every paired paint atom agrees in paint, style, shape, and delta; the measured persistent plus font-size mismatch is explicitly unsupported, proving one scene translation cannot repair the endpoint without a disallowed per-atom adaptation.

slices.title: generic-alignment-application
slices.summary: Intentionally applied no runtime correction. The measured endpoint fails the approved common-translation gate because only the persistent plus needs font-scale and baseline adaptation; adding that per-atom behavior would violate the preservation boundary. Native DOM and compositor playback remain unchanged, and the endpoint jerk is retained as a bounded known risk.

slices.title: endpoint-regression-matrix
slices.summary: Added explicit endpoint residual ceilings and a wide DPR1/phone DPR2 matrix covering font readiness, resize reload, direct seek, reverse, and repeated play. Focused tests, typecheck, 32 Chromium checks, stable 24-frame capture, isolated performance budgets, and reader production closure pass. The known 99.9 percent oversized-plus overlap remains visible but deterministic and bounded; native 100 percent settlement stays exact.

slices.title: endpoint-decision-record
slices.summary: Published the endpoint decision: the jerk is a deterministic persistent-plus font-scale and baseline mismatch, not handoff timing or rule geometry. One common translation cannot fix it, so no runtime exception was added. Numeric/browser/visual/performance/production/build gates bound the retained visual risk, native 100 percent settlement remains exact, and the review inbox contains no note for this experiment.
